date: Nov 21, 2026 · Week 2 / Day 6 · Decision-driven meetings and tradeoffs

cards.title: Sequence the calls
cards.question: A Gen5 channel needs either a retimer or a stackup change. Mechanical clearance is unresolved. Which decision comes first?
cards.selfCheck: Resolve the constraint that eliminates options before committing resources. Name the owner and decision deadline.
cards.prompt: Role-play a mechanical lead and program manager. Ask me to sequence the retimer versus stackup decisions, identify dependencies and deliver a 30-second recommendation.

cards.title: Invite the strongest objection
cards.question: Your team favors release despite marginal PCIe BER evidence. How do you uncover risks that consensus may hide?
cards.selfCheck: Ask for the strongest counterargument and evidence that would change the call. Record dissent and the disposition.
cards.prompt: Role-play a release review with a skeptical validation engineer. Challenge my recommendation and coach me to surface dissent without derailing the decision.

cards.title: Buy information, not simulations
cards.question: A PDN resonance has three plausible causes. You have four hours before the ECO deadline. Which investigation deserves resources?
cards.selfCheck: Choose the test most likely to change the ECO decision in time. State what you will do for each outcome.
cards.prompt: Give me three plausible PDN resonance hypotheses and competing tests. Make me choose based on decision value, time and fallback rather than technical curiosity.

cards.title: Resolve surprises before the room
cards.question: A crosstalk reroute consumes routing space reserved for another interface. How do you prepare for the design review?
cards.selfCheck: Pre-align with affected owners on constraints and acceptable alternatives. Bring unresolved tradeoffs to the decision maker.
cards.prompt: Role-play separate conversations with the layout and competing interface leads. Coach me to negotiate shared criteria and a concise decision request without authority.

cards.title: Update the call when facts change
cards.question: A conditional EM/TDR signoff depended on correlation within 3 ohms. New data shows a 5-ohm mismatch. What do you tell leadership?
cards.selfCheck: Reopen the agreed gate; explain the changed evidence, release exposure and next action. Exercise: deliver a 20-second update.
cards.prompt: Act as a director who already approved conditional signoff. Challenge my 20-second update on the failed correlation criterion, decision ownership, fallback and checkpoint.
